clue.text: Needle for decoration on artificial silk

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: something artificial is made up, so the letters of silk are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A sewing needle meant for embroidering rayon or other fake silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' suggests sewing, but it is the stone monument; 'artificial' is the anagram signal, giving LISK.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needle in London is a famous stone pillar of this tapering, four-sided kind.

clue.text: Important contract gets scornful response

explanation.surface: A major deal is greeted with a sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a large agreement, and idiomatically a dismissive exclamation belittling something.

clue.text: House deposit

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to accommodate or put up
as a verb, to place or ... something somewhere, such as a complaint or money

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs: to accommodate someone, and to place or file something formally.

clue.text: Glorious rendering of "Under the Linden Tree"

parts.note: the prefix sub- means under, as in submarine
the linden is another name for the lime tree

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderful performance of a song titled after a linden tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a song to be performed; really its words are taken one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of supreme excellence or beauty, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Relatives get a quarter — sighs of relief!

parts.note: NE, northeast, is a quarter of the compass
'phew' is the exclamation of relief, here plural

explanation.surface: Family members receive a share of an inheritance, and everyone breathes easier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's sons are relations, a plural example of family members.

clue.text: She can turn out to be an upper-class niece

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can turn out, rearranged, as something else

explanation.surface: A girl may prove to be a posh relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can turn out to be' rearranges U plus NIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so any woman bearing it can be called she.

clue.text: Breathe in, when gone to sleep in winter

indicators.note: the letters of the two words, once gone wrong or awry, are re-formed

explanation.surface: Breathing advice for drifting off on a cold night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when gone' rearranges the letters of BREATHE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as bears and hedgehogs pass the cold months in a dormant state, which is this verb.

clue.text: Wiped the floor with woollen fabric

definitions.meaning: a smooth cloth of tightly spun long-staple wool

explanation.surface: Mopping the floor with a woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb for defeating soundly, and the name of a fine wool cloth.

clue.text: Being wise, resigned

definitions.meaning: showing the wisdom of a thinker

explanation.surface: A wise person who has given up.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both learned reflection and stoical acceptance of bad luck.

clue.text: Agreed, but not about being old

indicators.note: the first word is taken but without the piece that follows

parts.note: RE is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone accepted a deal, though not about being elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: elderly, advanced in years.

clue.text: Where publicans are locked up?

parts.note: publicans work behind the bar of a pub; the phrase also means in prison

explanation.surface: Asking where pub landlords might be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in prison, and literally describes landlords standing at their counters.

clue.text: The old soldiers before one are Arabians

indicators.note: the soldiers come ahead of the numeral in the answer

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
men is a common word for soldiers or troops
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Veteran troops rank ahead of a single Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: People from a country on the Arabian peninsula; the word serves as a plural noun too.

clue.text: Slash the price of flimsy material

parts.note: lace is a delicate open fabric
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A shop cuts what it charges for a thin fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash the price' reads as cutting a cost, but 'Slash' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or cut skin roughly is a close synonym of a slashing wound.

clue.text: Delayed entering aisle, distressed, being nervous

indicators.note: one word goes into the other
distressed letters are shaken into another form

parts.note: late means delayed or behind time

explanation.surface: A latecomer squeezing along a theatre aisle, upset and anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' makes ILASE, and 'entering' splits that word so the delay sits in its middle; 'being' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means uncomfortable and anxious, a synonym for jittery.

clue.text: Teach unit members to become trustworthy

indicators.note: the member letters of the two words are made to become a new word by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Instruct a team's members to be reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members to become' rearranges the letters of TEACH UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and reliable, as a document or source that can be trusted.

clue.text: The Irish Bill?

parts.note: the Old Bill is British slang for the police; this is Ireland's equivalent force

explanation.surface: Asks about a piece of Irish legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Old Bill' is British slang for the police; here 'Bill' is that, not a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland's national police force goes by this name, matching the slang for constabulary.

clue.text: Dock, where a sailor may sleep

definitions.meaning: to moor a ship at a quay

explanation.surface: A sailor's sleeping place in port.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a mooring place for a vessel and a bunk in a ship's cabin.

clue.text: The embodiment of a mince pie, in my opinion

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters of pie are chopped and reordered

parts.note: 'to me' means in my view

explanation.surface: Someone declares a mince pie the perfect example of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the pastry's name, but it scrambles PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example or personification of a quality, a synonym.

clue.text: Describing insects with wings of short span

definitions.meaning: relating to mayflies, the winged insect order Ephemeroptera

explanation.surface: A description of winged insects with brief lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayflies, whose adults live a day, give the word for anything short-lived.

clue.text: Sort of seat for a high-flyer

definitions.text: Sort of seat for a high-flyer

parts.words: Sort of seat for a high-flyer
parts.note: a pilot's emergency seat that blasts out of the aircraft

explanation.surface: A seat for an ambitious achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'high-flyer' sounds like a go-getter, but it is a jet pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Military jets have a seat that propels the pilot clear in an emergency.

clue.text: Sinatra, swinging expert

indicators.note: the singer's name swings about, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Sinatra, the swing singer, was a master of his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled craftsperson, someone expert in a manual trade.

clue.text: A girl that is under another

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: another girl, a lass
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: One girl ranks below another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second girl, LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern word for a young woman.

clue.text: The intelligentsia left going over the same thing again? It's not on

indicators.note: the word on is not included, so it is removed

parts.words: going over the same thing again
parts.note: iteration is repetition of a process

explanation.surface: Clever people walking out of a repetitive debate in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes ON from ITERATION, giving ITERATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated, learned people interested in literature, a synonym for the intellectual class.

clue.text: Right sort of stock

explanation.surface: The proper type of shares to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Means fairness, and in finance names ordinary shares in a company.

clue.text: Availing oneself of an American gin sling

parts.note: US abbreviates United States, so American

indicators.note: to sling is to toss about, so the letters of gin are thrown around

explanation.surface: Drinking an American cocktail made with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin sling is a cocktail; here 'sling' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making use of something is a direct synonym of taking advantage of it.

clue.text: Rival to study before exam — an exemplary worker

indicators.note: the study comes ahead of the exam

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a test is an exam
the ant is the proverbial model of hard work

explanation.surface: A competitor revises for an exam like a model employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a contest is a rival to the others.

clue.text: In a way, it may mean this month

parts.note: St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A remark that something, in a sense, could signify the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: Old business letters wrote 'the 5th inst.' for the fifth of the present month.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation of instant, used formally to denote the present calendar period.

clue.text: Every setback about it is instructive

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the other

parts.note: the word set taken back, written backwards
each means every

explanation.surface: Each failure carries a useful lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like a failure but means SET read back, TES, which goes 'about' EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that instructs is giving lessons, so the verb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Naval jail and potential inmate

parts.note: a brig is a ship's prison

explanation.surface: A ship's prison and the outlaw who might end up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a criminal who could well end up behind prison walls.
